name: Diwali
description: The festival of lights celebrates the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. Homes are decorated with diyas, rangoli and lights.

name: Holi
description: The festival of colours celebrates the arrival of spring through colours, music, dance and community celebrations.

name: Durga Puja
description: A grand celebration honouring Goddess Durga, famous for artistic pandals, traditional rituals, music and cultural performances.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: A festival celebrating Lord Ganesha with beautifully decorated idols, prayers, music and community processions.

name: Navratri
description: Nine nights dedicated to Goddess Durga, celebrated with Garba, Dandiya Raas, traditional clothing and devotional music.

name: Baisakhi
description: A major Punjabi harvest festival marking the beginning of the harvest season, celebrated with Bhangra, Giddha and community gatherings.

name: Lohri
description: A winter harvest celebration featuring bonfires, folk songs, traditional dances, peanuts, popcorn and rewri.

name: Onam
description: Kerala's major harvest festival, celebrated with flower carpets, traditional feasts, boat races and cultural performances.

name: Pongal
description: A four-day Tamil harvest festival expressing gratitude to the Sun, cattle and nature for a successful harvest.

name: Bihu
description: Rongali Bihu marks the Assamese New Year and the agricultural season with traditional Bihu dance, songs and celebrations.

name: Hornbill Festival
description: A vibrant festival showcasing the traditions, music, dances, crafts and cuisines of Nagaland's diverse Naga tribes.

name: Losar
description: The Tibetan Buddhist New Year, celebrated with prayers, traditional dances, family gatherings and monastery ceremonies.

name: Tawang Festival
description: A celebration of Monpa culture featuring traditional dances, local food, handicrafts and cultural performances.

name: Chapchar Kut
description: A traditional Mizo spring festival celebrated with the Cheraw bamboo dance, folk music and community festivities.

name: Wangala Festival
description: The Garo harvest festival, also called the Hundred Drums Festival, celebrates the Sun God with rhythmic drums and traditional dances.

name: Desert Festival
description: A colourful celebration of Rajasthani heritage featuring folk music, Kalbelia dance, camel events and traditional costumes.

name: Pushkar Camel Fair
description: A famous annual fair combining livestock trading, traditional performances, competitions and religious activities.

name: Jagannath Rath Yatra
description: A major pilgrimage festival in Puri where Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are carried in grand decorated chariots.

name: Krishna Janmashtami
description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna, especially in Mathura and Vrindavan, with devotional songs, prayers and Dahi Handi events.

name: Chhath Puja
description: A traditional festival dedicated to the Sun God, involving offerings and prayers at rivers and water bodies during sunrise and sunset.

name: Ugadi
description: The Telugu New Year, celebrated with traditional food, festive decorations, prayers and the preparation of Ugadi Pachadi.

name: Gudi Padwa
description: The Marathi New Year, celebrated by raising decorated Gudi flags, preparing festive food and welcoming prosperity.

name: Vishu
description: A traditional Malayalam New Year celebration featuring Vishukkani arrangements, family gatherings and festive meals.

name: Mim Kut
description: A traditional Mizo festival associated with the maize harvest, remembered through community gatherings and offerings.

name: Kharchi Puja
description: A significant Tripuri religious festival involving worship of fourteen deities and traditional community celebrations.
